title: WordTwiq: the interaction and audio fixes after an AI-assisted Unity game became playable
author: Fabulous_Property452
selftext:
The hardest part of building my word puzzle with GPT 6 Astra in Codex turned out to be the small things around the game.



WordTwiq is a Unity/C# puzzle: two hidden five-letter words, one changed position, seven shared guesses. Each guess is scored against both answers. The tutorial pair is SHORE / SCORE. It's free to try in a browser: [https://wordtwiq.dfrankiej.com](https://wordtwiq.dfrankiej.com)



I directed the mechanics and visual revisions while Codex helped implement and review the game, the Mac build and the PWA. The first working version wasn't the end: a desktop layout that looked good was cramped on phones, editing a profile could leave Safari zoomed in, and a victory cue made the background music sound interrupted. Those became specific reproduction cases, then fixes and regression checks.



One audio change that helped: keep the licensed music playing and use a brief unpitched, beat-aligned accent for a result, rather than overlaying another musical phrase and dipping the whole song. The five selectable melodies are licensed Kevin MacLeod tracks, not AI-generated compositions. The WT icon artwork uses image generation; credits are in the game.



I'd appreciate a real playtest of one puzzle. Is the link between the two words clear? Does the second solve feel earned, or too obvious once the first is found? And does the result sound belong with the selected track? Browser/device details help if you hit a problem.



I'm DFrankieJ, the creator (DFRANKIEJ PRODUCTIONS). Google sign-in is optional. Feedback here, or wordtwiq@dfrankiej.com.
